A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TON research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material such as v1 Appendix G.10 to v3 Appendix I.

before.justification: V1 reports original TON experiments on CLEVR, Super-CLEVR, GeoQA and AITZ, including accuracy, output length, training time and ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds GSM8K results, a difficulty-aware dropout comparison and further qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The proposed reverse-thinking data generation, random thought-dropout SFT and subsequent GRPO procedure remain unchanged. Difficulty-aware dropout is evaluated as an alternative in an ablation, not adopted as a replacement component.

E1.justification: V3 adds actual text-only mathematical reasoning evaluation on GSM8K, extending coverage beyond the vision-language and GUI tasks in v1. CLEVR, Super-CLEVR, GeoQA and AITZ remain; the additional appendix examples mostly concern these already covered tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 6(c) adds difficulty-aware dropout as a comparator to TON's random dropout on GeoQA. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged; the GSM8K experiment extends the existing base-model and GRPO comparison pattern.

E3.justification: The new GSM8K experiment uses a distilled 1.5B Qwen model and reports pass@1 accuracy and average thought length. Section 5.3 additionally defines difficulty bands using base-model accuracy and tests dropping thoughts only for correctly answered examples. Previously documented benchmark protocols and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds the difficulty-aware versus random dropout ablation and an explicit comparison of task difficulty with skipping behavior in Figure 6. Appendix J adds selected GeoQA, Super-CLEVR and AITZ case studies, while Appendix I expands diagnostics for the existing length-reward experiment. Earlier dropout-rate and prompting ablations remain.

E5.justification: New Figure 6(a) displays error bars on accuracy and skip-ratio bars. Their statistical meaning and calculation are not explained, and no repeated-run counts or seeds are supplied. This changes uncertainty presentation without establishing that additional runs were performed.

E6.justification: V3 substantially broadens the reported results into text-only reasoning: Figure 6(b) reports GSM8K pass@1 of 78.7%, 81.4% and 82.3% for Qwen, GRPO and TON, with respective average thought lengths of 939, 978 and 342. Figure 6(c) adds 50.5% accuracy for difficulty-aware dropout versus 51.0% for random dropout, and Appendix J adds qualitative outcomes. Existing numerical results in Tables 2, 3, 5 and 9 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formalization, reverse-thinking expression, GRPO advantage and objective equations, and reward definitions are retained. V3 adds no theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the claimed applicability to LLM, VLM and agent tasks. The introduction also explicitly claims TON is the first work studying 'when to think' in VLMs. The central two-stage contribution and up-to-90% completion-length reduction claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the GSM8K result as evidence of generalization across modalities and suggests that difficulty heuristics may introduce noise or bias, explaining the preference for random dropout. The existing limitations concerning larger models and proprietary VLMs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 identifies the GSM8K model as Qwen2.5-1.5B-distill-deepseek-r1 and explains the correct-answer filter used for difficulty-aware dropout. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware, prompts and code-access information are retained. A detailed GSM8K training and evaluation recipe is not supplied.

R1.justification: V3 adds the GSM8K reference, Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems, and an explicit first-work novelty claim concerning selective reasoning in VLMs. The related-work discussion and other cited works are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and experimental discussion receive targeted additions, while most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. The appendix gains sections H–J, with the former length-reward subsection moved to I; affiliation and acknowledgement text also change.

P2.justification: The visual material expands substantially through the three-panel Figure 6, additional training displays and diagnostic panels, and the new qualitative figures and Super-CLEVR table in Appendix J. Table 1 gains a model-category column and GSM8K row. Original figures are largely retained, with some relocation, relabeling and repeated presentation of skip-ratio curves.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful evidence of text-only applicability and directly tests the previously untested choice between random and difficulty-aware dropout, while preserving the original method and results. The gains are limited by sparse GSM8K protocol details, unexplained error bars and an interpretation of heuristic bias that is not established by the reported 0.5-point accuracy difference.
